title: The Book of Rites, Part II
dateDisplay: Compiled c. 5th century BCE–1st century CE
attributionNote: The second half of the Li Ki continues the compilation of separate treaties on rites, music, mourning and the state of the empire, edited in the Han and transmitted with Zheng Xuan's commentary.
description: Books XI to XLVI of the Record of Rites: the jade-bead pendants and the places in the hall of distinction, the great treatise, the smaller and greater records of mourning, the law and meaning of sacrifices, Confucius at home at ease, the record of the dykes, the state of equilibrium and harmony, the meaning of capping, marriage, archery and the banquet, and the four principles underlying the mourning rites. This volume carries books XI to XLVI.
historicalContext: Zheng Xuan's second-century edition and commentary fixed the text, which supplied the ritual chapters of the imperial codes. Legge's translation of the second half forms volumes 28 of the Sacred Books of the East (1885).
availabilityNote: Complete: books XI to XLVI in Legge's translation, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed book per chapter. The volume's title page and Legge's notes are volume apparatus and are not part of the work.
